usual_baseline: Pathways exist but key steps are missed. In Scotland 36% of units had ERAS and 35% of patients were catheterised [1263]. 66.0% mobilised within 24 hours after TKR [1535]. Same-day discharge 54.3% after THA [1539]. Mean length of stay 3.6 days for hips and knees [1387].
fix_that_works: National steering group: units with ERAS 36% to 68%, catheterisation 35% to 26% [1263]. MDT group with parallel PDSA cycles: length of stay 3.6 to 2.4 days for hips and 2.0 for knees, all mobilised on day 0 [1387]. MDT feedback: mobilisation within 24 hours 66.0% to 90.5% [1535]. Order set plus spinal lidocaine: same-day discharge 54.3% to 80.6% [1539].
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. Median length of stay stayed at 2 days despite better mobilisation, and no day 0 physiotherapy was documented [1535]. Unscheduled 30-day encounters did not change, 10.5% to 9.3% [1539].
consultant_advice: Not overdone; only five audits here. Mobilisation and length of stay are the usual measures. More useful: pain as the barrier to mobilisation, which was linked to a 5.2-day stay [1535], and 30-day returns alongside discharge targets.
